I've been farming this land since I was a girl helping my parents. My husband went to work in Baoding three years ago, so I manage the fields myself now, about 8 mu. I don't take risks with new things I don't understand.

Here in Quzhou, everyone grows wheat in winter and maize in summer. That's what this land is for. The county seed station sells improved wheat varieties — Shimai or Jimai — and I'll buy from them again like I always do. For maize, I'll get Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed from the agri-supply shop in town. Everyone uses it, the yield is reliable.

For wheat, I put down compound fertilizer as base when I till in October, then urea top-dressing in spring when it starts jointing. I irrigate three times: the winter water before freezing, the jointing water in April, and the grain-filling water in May. I spray herbicide in winter and fungicide/insecticide around heading — the extension station sends messages telling us when.

For maize after wheat harvest in June, I just direct-seed into the stubble — no need to till again. I apply base fertilizer and urea when it's knee-high. Summer rain usually handles irrigation but I'll pump once if July is dry. Spray for fall armyworm if needed.

I'll sell grain to the county grain station. The price isn't great but it's guaranteed.
